newsitem.title: USA: FIGURE SKATING-KWAN LEADS AFTER WOMEN'S SHORT PROGRAM.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-KWAN LEADS AFTER WOMEN'S SHORT PROGRAM.

text.p: Michelle Kwan
recovered from a mistep after a double axel to lead the
women's competiton after the women's short programme with nine
out of nine first place votes at the U.S. Figure Skating
Championships on Friday.
Tiny Tara Lipinski, 14, was second and 26-year old Tara
Kwaitkowski was third.
Kwaitkowski, the defending silver medalist, held second
place through most of the 21 skaters.
But the 4'8" (1.42 meters) Lipinski impressed the judges
by including the more difficult triple lutz-double loop in her
programme than Kwaitkowski's triple-lutz-double toe combination.
While both Kwaitkowski and Lipinski have developed an
impressive resume of international medals this competition
season, Friday night at the Nashville Arena was the first time
this season the two faced off in direct competition.
Last year, Kwaitkowski finished eighth at the Worlds.
Lipinski, making her international debut, was 15th.
Nicole Bobek, the 1995 bronze medalist at the World
championships and the U.S. National Champion, was sixth.
Bobek did not receive full credit for her triple
lutz-double toe because she took an extra step to complete the
combination, and she also lost points when she executed a
double toe jump instead of the required triple.
"You just have to concentrate on one thing at time," Kwan
said. "Sometimes I can't sleep I'm so excited thinking 'next
year is the Olympics,' then I realise I still have Nationals
and I can sleep."
Since Kwan's world championship last March, she has won
the Japan Open, the Ultimate Four Challenge, France's Trophy
Lalique, Skate America, and the Continents Cup.
"I was pleased, this is the first time she's defended her
title" Kwan's coach Frank Carroll said. "The short programme is
a killer in our sport."
